reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and friendly! The lectures were intuitive and helped me learn some hard concepts. Takes time to explain matter at a gentle pace. The course was only homework and project so class participation mattered. Would take again.

Main issue: grading transparency. The final project rubric looked clear, but in practice it was broad and highly subjective. I got a much lower grade than expected with almost no specific feedback. Strong technical work alone may not be enough here—presentation polish and instructor fit seem to matter a lot.

To be honest, I wasn't feeling great going into this class at the beginning of the sem, but Guha made the class very manageable. Grade split is 80% exam/ 20% Homework, the midterms were moderately difficult since they were short multiple choice but you can use a cheat sheet which helps alot. Homeworks are not bad. Final was the same as the practice
Cares about the students' learning experience, often explains topics multiple times if needed without being asked to make sure students really understand the material

Only 4 homeworks, with the length decreasing as the semester went on (she extended deadlines for the class as well). Midterms were very similar to the reviews she gave (you go through the reviews in class with her), and the final was nearly identical to the final review. Goated prof.

Lecture is proof heavy but not mandatory so not many people showed up. Homeworks are all about R and aren't too difficult. Allows a cheat sheet for exams. The first 2 exams are moderately difficult only because they're about 9 questions each. The final was almost the exact same as the practice.

At first, I was scared of going to class after failing STAT 211 and knowing that 212 is more advanced, but she did an amazing job that my 211 prof couldn't. She clearly explained things much better and made us understand the material bit by bit. Got an A in the class :). Best STAT prof ever :)

Clearly she changed things up since previous semesters as now attendance is required and the first two tests are no longer just copies of the practice tests. The final however was copy pasted from the practice which made this class a very easy A.

Allows cheat sheets on exams. Practice exams are exactly like exams (also, the other STAT 212 class had copy/paste our exam as their practice exam). My final was copy and pasted from the practice, which is what I made my cheat sheet from. For homework, GO TO THE TA office hours and you automatically get a 100.

The practice tests she releases are almost identical to the real tests. She will go over the practice tests in class and explain how she got to that answer. Overall, a pretty interesting class and she is very helpful.

If you can, TAKE HER! I'm not great at statistics at all, but she is a really good professor. Just do the exam reviews very well and you should be fine for the exams. Only 3 homework R assignments. Class isn't mandatory, but can be helpful to go to, especially before the exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't particularly interesting or necessary as exams have almost no theory on them. MC exams with cheat sheet allowed. Honestly, just going to class the week before exam to get the review and using that to formulate a cheat sheet works fine. Just make sure to read up on the lecture slides before homework time!
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very less work from her class. Would recommend the professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Guha is a super sweet prof! Sometimes lectures can be boring bc they are theory based, so attending isn't necessary but can be sometimes helpful. 
Very few hws given (roughly 5 for the sem) - low workload overall. 
For exams - do the practice exams! She allows a cheat sheet, so be thorough and you'll do well. 
Guha is the best option for STAT212!!!
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing. Dr. Guha was incredible at explaining things simply and at a gentle  pace. You don't need to attend every lecture but it was definitely worth it. She cares about the course, the students, and her work in Statistics. I wish I could have her for every course.

Honestly a very good professor. Her lectures focus more on theory than implementation, but the homework and practice exams are very helpful in applying. Get ready to use R on all of your homework. Exams weren't bad, especially if you use her practice exam and go in class for review sessions.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing teacher. I hate statistics. I barreled through Stats 211 barely understanding anything. After taking 212 with Dr Guha I feel like have a firm grasp on the concepts covered during class. Her lectures were excellent and the reviews accurately reflected what was on the exams. Take this teacher!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She does a GREAT job at explaining things. There were no quizzes only tests and homework. Her tests were not difficult if you completed the practice test. She makes 100% sure her students have understood the material before she moves to the next topic. Take this professor! If you pay attention in class and do the homework you can make a good grade.

one of the BEST professors I've had at TAMU! If you've had Dr. Tyagi for a CS course, she's a lot like him. ALWAYS responds to emails, cares about her students. puts A LOT of time and effort into making the lecture material easy to understand. doesn't put "trick" questions on exams, and tests students on their comprehension of the material.

She's very nice and accessible, I never have emailed her but I feel like if you did she would respond quickly. You can kinda tell that she's not here to teach though. However, it's not a hard class, the material is interesting, and it's not a lot of work compared to most other technical classes.

Although this was her first semester teaching, it didn't feel like it. The lectures were good with here taking her time and explaining concepts and formulas. She answers all questions you ask her during class. There were only 3 tests but they were very simple and straight forward if you do the provided review. Would recommend taking her class.
